column1: # The diagnostic codes: the source of truth for self/diag/codes_gen.maxon.
# Run `go generate ./internal/...` after an edit. Columns, separated by tabs:
#   constant   the name, which self/ spells with a lower-case first letter
#   code       the code in the rows' ascending order; the stage digit is 1 lexer, 2 parser, 3 semantic, 4 IR, 9 internal
#   maxon      the case of ErrorCode in maxon-bin/Compiler/ErrorCodeRegistry.maxon that has this number, or - for a code
#              of minimaxon's own; `diaggen --maxon <maxon repository>` checks both against the registry
# A code of minimaxon's own takes a number from E3900 (semantic) or E9900 (internal), which maxon does not use.

column4: An escape in a literal is malformed, or a byte string holds a character that is no byte.
The parser met a token that cannot appear at this point.
A type is needed of a kind the name does not have: a typealias implements a ranged typealias.
An expression is not well formed or not usable where it stands.
The parser reached the end of the file with a construct still open.
A block's 'end' label does not match the label its header opened.
A specific token was required here.
An integer literal is outside every type it could have.
Something is defined in terms of itself: modules, constants or typealiases in a cycle.
An assignment targets something that cannot be reassigned.
The source uses a construct this compiler does not implement, such as a static function outside a type.
A match arm that returns also says 'and fallthrough'.
A match covers neither every case of its subject nor a default.
A match arm or a ternary branch has a type that the others do not, or a pattern does not match its subject.
A constant's initializer is not known at compile time.
The default arm of a match over an enum or union does not panic.
A match arm's action is a block statement.
A call labels its first argument.
A call leaves a later argument without its label.
A shift's count is a negative constant.
A generic instance names the wrong number of type arguments.
A 'test' declaration is in a file whose name does not end in '.maxtest'.
A 'test' declaration has an empty name.
A '#if' has no '#endif', or an '#else' or '#endif' has no '#if'.
A '#if' condition calls a function that is not 'os', 'arch', 'testing', 'rcSanitize', 'leakReport' or 'debugstream'.
A '#if' condition is not a combination of predicate calls, or text follows it on its line.
A call labels an argument of a built-in function whose arguments are positional.
The count of a fixed array is not an integer literal from 1 to 4294967295.
A qualified name names a member its base does not declare.
A project file lies below another project's directory, and projects do not nest.
A method or a requirement is named where a function value is needed.
The program declares no 'main' function.
'main' returns a type other than ExitCode.
A call names a function or method that does not exist.
A value's type is not the type required where it stands.
A name is declared twice where only one declaration is allowed.
A declaration is named from a module its visibility does not reach.
A cast or a conversion between number types that loses what the value is: a float to an integer.
A named type resolves to no declared type.
A function that returns a value can reach its end without returning one.
A field is read or written from a module its visibility does not reach.
A type says it implements an interface but lacks or mismatches a member.
A type argument does not meet the bound its type parameter declares.
A field access names a field the type does not have.
An enum declares a case name twice.
Two cases of an enum have the same raw value.
The raw values of an enum or a union are not all of one kind: integers, floats or strings.
A name is not a case of its enum or union.
A match pattern binds a different number of values than its case carries.
A call passes a different number of arguments than the callee takes.
A call's label names no parameter of the callee.
Two arguments of one call are for the same parameter.
'main' is declared 'throws', with no caller to handle the error.
A call that can fail is made without 'try' where nothing catches the failure.
An error goes where nothing takes an error of its type: a 'try' or 'throw' with no caller to pass it to, or one that throws another.
A typealias is declared twice in one type's body.
A union is compared with '==' or '!='.
An operand of 'is' or 'is not' has no object identity: a number, a bool, an enum case, a union, a function or a type parameter.
A match arm names a case of an enum or union with its type's name, which the subject already gives.
A struct literal is written outside the methods of its type.
A block other than a function body holds no statement.
The handler of a try block names the error but never matches on it.
A struct literal omits a field that has no default.
A typealias refers back to itself through the aliases it implements, or an interface through the interfaces it extends.
A function that throws is used as a value, which no function type can hold.
A name is read after its value was moved out of it.
A division or 'mod' has a constant zero divisor.
An array is created with zeroed elements of a type that has no zero value.
Two tests of a module have names that compile to one symbol.
A 'throws' clause names something other than an enum or a union.
A method call on a type parameter names a method that more than one of its bounds declares.
A static requirement of an interface is called through a type parameter, which has no receiver to dispatch on.
An 'if try' with no binding tests a call that returns a value, which it discards.
A type argument implements its bound's interface, but binds an associated type to another type than the bound names.
A bits(n) typealias has a width the language does not have.
A source file outside the runtime calls a __Raw intrinsic.
A declaration's signature names a type less visible than the declaration.
A typealias implements one whose range does not hold its own, or that is over another primitive or signedness.
A type parameter of a generic function is fixed by no argument.
A directory of the program cannot be spelled as a module name.
A field of a generic type holds that type again over a type built from its own parameters, so its instances never end.
An argument handed to a written parameter overlaps another operand of the call.
An instance method is called by its type's name or, in a static method, by its bare name, with no value to call it on.
A fixed array's create takes a length its type does not need, or lacks one it does.
A write or a consuming call goes through the contents of a frozen value.
A function value writes what it captured, which its function type does not allow.
An unsigned value is negated.
The initializer of a constant calls a function.
'main' declares parameters.
A borrowed value is moved somewhere that would own it.
A part of a value is moved out of a value that stays in use.
A name is read before it has a value.
A 'sets' parameter is unnamed or is not given a value on every path.
An argument for a 'sets' parameter already has a value.
An interface that cannot be the type of a value, since a requirement names Self or is static, names one.
A generic function instantiates itself with a type argument that grows without end.
A type parameter, bound or 'implements' clause is declared where it is not allowed.
A type that cannot be a map key is used as one.
A behaviour keeps a borrowed value, which it outlives.
'freeze' is applied to a plain value that is copied freely.
'share' or 'thaw' is given a value of the wrong kind: not a frozen value, or not a cown reference.
A 'when' names something that is not a cown, or names and binds a different number of them.
A 'when' names one cown twice.
A cown can reach itself, so a cycle of references would exist.
The value of a cown is used outside a behaviour that holds the cown.
A constraint names a type parameter its declaration does not have.
A typealias names something other than an integer range or a generic instance.
A value of a type that is not Copyable is copied.
A value of a type that is not Droppable is dropped without a destructor.
A destructor is declared on a type that has nothing to end, or is passed 'self' where only another destructor may take it.
An argument naming a type's capability is wrong for the type it is given.
A value of a type with destructors is taken apart outside them.
A function that takes a 'sets' parameter declares 'throws'.
A function value that holds a borrow escapes it: it is stored, returned, consumed, copied or captured by something that may outlive the borrow.
A raw value is a string with an interpolated value, which a case cannot hold.
Two declarations that a module sees say one type implements one interface.
A call names a method that two extensions the calling module sees add to the type.
A type contains itself.
A construct the compiler does not support yet.
A construct only the interpreter runs, so no native code is made for it.
